answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral, turning the network into a frozen glacier of frozen value that renders identity replication prohibitively expensive. An attacker attempting to simulate a sonnet of bot accounts must acquire substantial native tokens, creating a cost function that scales linearly with influence. Much like the resilient yarrow plant, this economic threshold maintains structural integrity, as the financial penalty for Byzantine behavior ensures that gaining fake identities costs more than the potential yield.
